issues.description: Interface name mismatch: the problem statement (UML and prose) and the template Main use an interface named 'Rideable' with a method messageOnRide(), but the provided solution defines and uses an interface named 'Mountable' (Mountable.java) and leaves Rideable.java empty. In the solution, Pig and Seal implement Mountable (e.g., 'public class Pig ... implements Mountable'), while the specification and template expect Rideable. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual interface will confuse students and cause compilation errors when following the template/tests that reference Rideable.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Recommended approach preserving the problem statement and template: rename the solution's Mountable.java to Rideable.java (or update its file to declare 'public interface Rideable { String messageOnRide(); }'), update Pig.java and Seal.java to 'implements Rideable', and remove or replace the empty Rideable.java file in the solution. Alternatively, if you prefer Mountable as the canonical name, update the problem statement and template to refer to 'Mountable' everywhere. Ensure the interface signature (messageOnRide()) matches the specification so code and tests compile.
